segments.line: Your arm is in a cast. The
doctor holds your X- ray up to the light, and she goes very quiet.
'Your bones, ' she says. 'They're thicker than yesterday. A lot thicker. ' The
rule just broke. Your body is starting to catch up.
Then she asks the question nobody has asked yet. 'If your bones can change... what else is changing? '
Outside the window, the black car is back. Two of them now.
It's five fifty- nine. One minute until your alarm.
So, is any of this real? The doubling is. Fifty kilos, doubled twenty times, really is the Titanic.
Muscles really can break their own bones. And
lifting all that weight really would cost a mountain of food. And
super- strong kids exist. A rare change in a gene called myostatin lets muscles keep growing.
Doctors have described a baby boy born with unusually huge muscles. Just not doubling every day.
Would you go with the man in the suit, or run? Tell me in the comments.
